chunks: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
From what God revealed to Moses (peace be upon him) and sent down to him in the Torah was:

"I, I am God — there is no god except Me. I created the creatures and I created the good and caused it to flow upon the hands of those whom I love, so blessed is the one upon whose hands I caused it to flow."

"And I am God — there is no god except Me. I created the creatures and I created evil and caused it to flow upon the hands of those whom I intend, so woe to the one upon whose hands I caused it to flow."

key_terms.أجريته: I caused it to flow (ajraytuhu) — metaphor of good/evil as something channeled through human hands by divine will
key_terms.الخير: Good (khayr) — divine beneficence and blessing that flows through the divinely favored
key_terms.الشر: Evil (sharr) — adversity and corruption allowed to flow through those whom God wills to test or punish
key_terms.طوبى: Beatitude/blessedness (tuba) — a state of divine happiness and felicity for those through whom good flows
key_terms.ويل: Woe (wayl) — a curse or expression of divine displeasure and the punishment awaiting those through whom evil flows

ai.seo_question: What did God reveal to Moses about good and evil in the Torah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith reports Imam al-Sadiq's (peace be upon him) citation of a divine revelation to Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) contained in the Torah. The revelation presents a parallel theological statement affirming divine unity and the sovereignty of God over both good and evil — good flows through those whom God loves, while evil flows through those whom God wills or intends. The audience — early Shia Muslims grappling with theological questions about divine justice and determinism — would have understood this as an affirmation that God is the ultimate cause and sovereign over all creation, not as a denial of human moral responsibility, but as a statement of God's absolute omnipotence and foreknowledge.
